summary: Sean, after a draining visit to a noisy ward with his Grampa, checks into the Lamplighter Inn on a dreary Florida strip and listens to a useless voicemail from Caleb, which he cannot transcribe. At the motel pool he meets Adele, an elderly, sun-baked woman who warns him the chlorinated water is bad, recommends Universal over Disney, and chats about Canadian 'snowbirds' while Sean says he has work to do down south.
one_line: Sean, a Toronto visitor in Florida, checks into a seedy motel and meets the talkative elderly guest Adele at the pool.
key_facts: Sean checks into the Lamplighter Inn, located on a dreary strip populated with disused water-parks and crumbling plazas.
The Lamplighter Inn is the first motel Sean finds after leaving the ward.
Sean plays back a recording in which a message from Caleb says, "I'm lactose intolerant."
The noise of the ward masked nine words in ten of the recording, and Sean found the surviving words empty of emotional freight.
Sean finds the motel pool water piss-warm and thickly chlorinated, feeling like swimming in pungent sweat.
Adele is an old, old woman wearing a one-piece with a skirt and a sunhat, with skin the color and texture of rawhide.
Adele says the pool's owner, Old Ross, doesn't like dealing with the pool and keeps shoveling in chlorine, so guests may be blonde in the morning.
Adele tells Sean that Universal is better than Disney in her opinion, and that most people don't bother with it.
Sean tells Adele he is visiting from Toronto and has a lot of work to do down south.
Sean says he will not get a chance to visit Universal or the other parks because of his work.
Adele calls visitors from Toronto 'snowbirds' who come to Florida to escape winter and then complain about the heat.
Sean's work relates to a thesis proposal, for which he has rehearsed a high-concept speech many times.
Sean is staying in Florida for a few weeks, at least, according to his own statement to Adele.
